Q: How does serial console communication work in a microcontroller? A:

There are two possibilities.

  1. You connect to a USB/UART bridge such as devices made by FTDI or Prolific,
  2. The microcontroller has a USB device controller and USB stack implementing the CDC/ACM device class (virtual COM port).

In the first instance, the bridge chip presents the CDC/ACM device to the host and exchanges data with a UART connected to the microcontroller UART. I/O control such as setting the baud rate have no impact on the USB connection, rather they are used to configure the UART link.

In the bridge arrangement, the bridge chip may be on the micro board, or it may be in a USB/serial adapter cable. Moreover internally the bridge chip is a microcontroller with a CDC/ACM device stack.

Unlike say RS-232, USB is not a peer-to-peer full duplex connection, and is not merely an electrical connection; USB requires quite complex device and host controllers and is more analogous to a device bus such as PCI than it is to UART serial connections. A CDC/ACM class device conforms to a specific protocol to allow a "virtual" UART to appear at the host. The UART you see at the PC is emulated, and is not physically the UART in the bridge.

The physical actual USB connection is a master-slave connection, with data and I/O control commands (such as baud rate and flow control) sent in USB packets to be unpacked, interpreted and transferred to the application layer via the CDC/ACM USB stack. In this arrangement the device, acting as a slave cannot initiate an exchange; rather the host continuously polls the device to which the device may return a packet containing its "tx" data. The polling and data rate of USB are fast enough to allow the simplex master-slave exchange to emulate a full-duplex UART connection, at higher throughput than can normally be achieved by a typical real UART, and certainly faster than a physical RS-xxx connection.

You can get an idea of how all this works by observing the raw USB data exchange using a tool such as WireShark. You will see that a lot more than just your application "serial" data is being exchanged.

Q: What skills and technologies should i learn to become a data scientist A:

I think so

Months 1-2: Build a Solid Foundation
Focus on mastering Python programming (with an emphasis on Pandas and NumPy) along with mathematics and statistics fundamentals. This is the hard prerequisite for all subsequent learning.

Months 3-5: Master Core Machine Learning
Systematically study the Scikit-learn library, and gain a deep understanding of classic models including linear regression, logistic regression, decision trees, SVM, and clustering. At the same time, master core evaluation concepts such as cross-validation and the bias-variance tradeoff.

Months 6-8: Dive into Deep Learning
Start with the basics of neural networks, then progressively learn Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for image processing and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) for sequential data (e.g., text, time series). These are essential skills for AI research positions.

Months 9-10: Hands-on Projects
Apply what you've learned in practice. Choose a complete project on platforms like Kaggle, and go through the entire pipeline from data cleaning to modeling and evaluation. Document the whole process (code, approach, results) and publish it on GitHub — this will be your best resume.

Months 11-12: Explore Research Frontiers
If you're aiming for AI research, start reading and attempting to reproduce research papers from top conferences such as NeurIPS and ICML. Make good use of websites like "Papers with Code" , which provide implementations alongside the papers — they are very helpful for getting started with reproduction.

Q: Return row numbers in Excel VBA - SQL A:

Calculate Item number with subquery

    strSQL = "SELECT [ID], Sum([QTY]) As myQTY,  Round(myTOTAL/myQTY,2) As myPRICE, Sum([TOTAL]) As myTOTAL " & _
            " ,(SELECT count(*) " & _
            "   FROM (SELECT Id FROM [ASDRT$] union SELECT Id FROM [FSR$])t2" & _
            "   WHERE t2.id< t.Id" & _
            "   )+1 As Item " & _
            "FROM " & _
             " ( " & _
             "   SELECT [ID], [QTY], [TOTAL] FROM [ASDRT$] " & _
             "   UNION ALL " & _
             "   SELECT [ID], [QTY], [TOTAL] FROM [FSR$] " & _
             " )t " & _
             "WHERE [ID]<>'' " & _
             "GROUP BY [ID]" & _
             "ORDER BY [ID]"

Item number calculation require "order" definition. In this example items ordered by Id. I added the order (ORDER BY) to the query.

(SELECT count(*) 
 FROM (SELECT Id FROM [ASDRT$] union SELECT Id FROM [FSR$]) t2
 WHERE t2.id< t.Id
 )+1 As Item

In words: count the number of IDs that are less than the current one.

Similar to

   SELECT dense_rank()over(order by Id) as Item
   FROM (SELECT Id FROM [ASDRT$] UNION SELECT Id FROM [FSR$]) t2

"UNION" is used in subquery, so Id's is unique and row_number() and dense_rank() will get same values.

Q: What are Python namespaces all about A:

So a namespace is basically a name + space. So its a space where names ( meaning variables, functions, classes, etc) are stored. This prevents naming conflicts that can arise when identical names are used, so different parts of a program can use the same name without interfering with each other. Python uses namespaces for modules, classes, and functions. This mainly is helpful for avoiding clashes with multiple identical names.

Hope this helped you

Q: Is tms web core pages rendered server side or client side? A:

TMS Webcore transpiles Delphi (pascal) to JavaScript. It produces an SPA (a single page app). This runs entirely in the browser.

All the html, CSS and JavaScript are already loaded into the browser. All rendering, therefore happens at the client. It is not like PHP, which is entirely server side.

From Pascal to Javascript Compiler

Scope and architecture
TMS WEB Core is based on compiling Delphi UI code to JavaScript and creating this way what is called Single-Page-Applications. The terminology "page" should not be confused with forms that Delphi developers are used to. A TMS WEB Core application can contain multiple forms. These multiple forms will be hosted in a JavaScript application a web browser user can navigate to via a single page URL.

Pascal to Javascript Compiler
For creating the single-page JavaScript application, the Pascal code of your project is compiled to JavaScript and this JavaScript application runs in the browser. . Typically a connection to the server will be made by HTTP REST requests or via WebSocket communication.

It is based on this open source project pas2js

Pas2js : What is it ?
Compiler
Pas2js is an open source Pascal to JavaScript transpiler. It parses Object Pascal and emits JavaScript. The JavaScript is currently of level ECMAScript 5 and should run in any browser or in Node.js (target "nodejs"). It is available in 5 forms:......

Q: Why does my net10.0 AspNetCore WebApi revert to VSTest in Linux pipeline A:

Change this:

dotnet test src/Authentication --no-build --coverlet --coverlet-file-prefix "authentication" --results-directory src/coverage

To this:

dotnet test src/Authentication --no-build --results-directory src/coverage -- --coverlet --coverlet-file-prefix "authentication"

You need to add a double-dash (--) before your Coverlet flags.

All parameters are passed to msbuild by the CLI. Without the --, MSBuild treats --coverlet and --coverlet-file-prefix as its own command-line switches, which causes the error. The -- tells the CLI to pass the flags directly to the Coverlet test runner.

The order has been shifted so that everything before the -- is processed by dotnet and msbuild. Everything after is given to the test runner as is.
